1.explanation: In MultiSelect.js we render <ListBox.Selection> (the clear-selection control) directly inside the <button> that toggles the dropdown. ListBox.Selection (implemented in ListBoxSelection.js) itself uses a <div role="button" tabIndex> and handles click/keydown, i.e. an interactive control. That nested interactive element is exactly what HTML5 forbids and what’s triggering the accessibility error. To fix this, either the toggle field should not be a <button> when it contains other interactive controls or the clear-selection control should render a non-interactive element (e.g., plain <span>) and delegate events to the parent button, thereby removing the nested button role.
1.bug_scenario: When a user opens our MultiSelect with one or more items selected, the clear-selection control (the “×” tag) is rendered inside the main toggle <button>. In the preview screenshots you can see the outer <button> (the MultiSelect field) containing an inner element with role="button" and tabIndex that also listens for clicks/keypresses – effectively a button inside a button. This violates the HTML5 spec requirement that a <button> may not have interactive content as a descendant, and it introduces accessibility errors and confusion for screen-reader/keyboard users.
